mainTopic: Defining the דרגש for an אבל, and how far a vow against a city or a house reaches
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of the דרגש, a kind of bed that an אבל (mourner) does not have to overturn. The גמרא first compares a 'fortune-bed' to a bed used only for storage, which is not overturned either. It then drops the fortune-bed idea, because רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a דרגש has loops, and רבין reports that a דרגש is a leather bed. Next the גמרא asks how a מטה differs from a דרגש. After a challenge from a משנה about smoothing wood with fish skin, it concludes that both are strung through the frame: a מטה through holes and a דרגש through loops. Two rulings close the bed topic: a bed with protruding posts is just stood on its side, and the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A new משנה then teaches that a vow against a city includes its עיבור but not its תחום, and a vow against a house begins at the doorstop. The גמרא proves the עיבור rule from יהושע being 'in יריחו' while the city was shut, and shows the תחום is 'outside the city.' Finally, רב מרי challenges the doorstop rule from the laws of a house with נגעים, and the גמרא answers that that case is different because of the special words 'from the house.'

steps.title: A fortune-bed is like a bed used only for storing things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why an אבל does not overturn a דרגש, if a דרגש is a fortune-bed: it is just like a bed used only for holding vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like a bed set aside for vessels. A ברייתא teaches: if the bed was set aside for vessels, the mourner does not need to overturn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked just before this: why is a דרגש (understood as a fortune-bed) not overturned in a house of mourning? It compares it to a bed used only for storage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל overturns beds that people use to lie on. A bed used only to hold vessels is not a sleeping bed, so it is not overturned. A fortune-bed is not slept on either, so it gets the same ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like… (a comparison formula)
A bed set aside for holding vessels, not for sleeping
To overturn it (the mourner's custom of turning beds over)

steps.confusionAlert: This step only makes sense with the previous line in mind: the גמרא had defined דרגש as an ערסא דגדא (fortune-bed). That definition is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: It is just like a bed designated for vessels,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the דרגש, which the גמרא just called a fortune-bed that nobody sleeps on.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אִם הָיְתָה מִטָּה הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים —
phrases.english: as it is taught: If it was a bed designated for vessels,
one does not need to overturn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question just before this, about why a fortune-bed is not overturned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an established case (a bed used only for vessels)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a דרגש is a kind of bed, an אבל should have to overturn it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bed not used for sleeping, like a storage bed or a fortune-bed, is not overturned.

steps.title: A fortune-bed would not have loops
steps.stepSummary: The real difficulty: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a דרגש has loops that can be untied. A fortune-bed would not have them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty. A ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: for a דרגש, the mourner unties its loops and it falls down by itself. But if a דרגש is a fortune-bed, does it have loops?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the overturning question was not the real problem. The real problem is a ברייתא showing that a דרגש has loops, which does not fit the idea of a fortune-bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes a דרגש as having loops that hold up the bedding, so loosening them makes it collapse. That describes a working bed built for lying on. A decorative fortune-bed would not be built this way, so the definition 'fortune-bed' looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if anything is difficult, this is what is difficult
Loops that tie the straps holding the bedding to the frame
A fortune-bed, set aside for good luck and not slept on

phrases.english: Rather, if something is difficult, this is difficult,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A dargash: he unties its loops
and it falls down by itself.
And if a dargash is a fortune-bed,
does it have loops?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts aside the overturning issue and raises a stronger challenge to the definition itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of דרגש as an ערסא דגדא (fortune-bed).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that a דרגש has loops for its bedding, which fits a real bed and not a fortune-bed.

steps.title: רבין's new definition: a leather bed
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רב תחליפא, who spent time in the tanners' market, told him that a דרגש is a leather bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: I asked one of the Sages, whose name was רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל and who was often found in the tanners' market. He told me: what is a דרגש? A leather bed.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge, the גמרא brings a new definition of דרגש from someone who knew leather goods well: it is a bed made with leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leather bed is a real bed, so it can have loops, and that fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The detail that רב תחליפא was found in the tanners' market explains why he would know this word.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A man from the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This replaces the fortune-bed definition. It now becomes the working definition of דרגש for the rest of the discussion.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
I asked a certain one of the Sages,
and Rav Tachlifa from the West was his name,
who was often found in the tanners' market,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לִי: מַאי דַּרְגֵּשׁ — עַרְסָא דְצַלָּא.
phrases.english: and he said to me: What is a dargash? A leather bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by replacing the definition of דרגש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A דרגש is a fortune-bed that nobody sleeps on.
steps.terutzMaskana: A דרגש is a leather bed, a real bed that can have loops.
steps.whatToRemember: The fortune-bed definition is dropped. A דרגש is a leather bed.

steps.title: What separates a מטה from a דרגש?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is stated: what exactly is the difference between a regular bed and a דרגש?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: which is a bed and which is a דרגש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants the exact construction difference between a regular bed and a דרגש. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are real beds now, so the גמרא needs a clear way to tell them apart. This matters for the משנה's vow, where רבי יהודה holds that someone who swore off a 'bed' may still use a דרגש, while the חכמים say a דרגש is included in 'bed'.

phrases.english: It was stated: Which is a bed and which is a dargash?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the new leather-bed definition by asking how it differs from a regular bed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical difference between a מטה and a דרגש.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: straps over the frame versus through the frame
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers: a מטה has its straps wrapped over the top of the frame, and a דרגש has them strung through the frame itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: a bed is strung with straps over its top. A דרגש is strung through its own body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the first answer. The difference is how the straps that hold the bedding are attached to the frame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מטה the straps wrap around the outside of the frame, so they cover the wood. In a דרגש the straps pass through the wood of the frame. This answer is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: They string or weave the straps (that hold the bedding)
Over its top, around the outside of the frame
Through its own body, meaning through the frame itself

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
A bed: one strings it over its top,
a dargash: one strings it through its own body.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מטה's straps wrap over the frame. A דרגש's straps go through the frame.

steps.title: Why smooth a bed's frame if the straps hide it?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a wooden bed can become טמא once it is smoothed with fish skin. If the straps cover the frame, why would that smoothing matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: from when can wooden vessels become טמא? A bed and a crib, from when he smooths them with fish skin. But if a bed is strung over its top, why do I need smoothing with fish skin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה using a משנה about when a wooden bed counts as a finished vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a bed is finished, and can become טמא, only once its wood is smoothed with fish skin. That final smoothing only makes sense if the wood can be seen. If the straps wrapped over the frame and hid it, nobody would bother smoothing it, so a regular bed must also be strung through the frame.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoothing or polishing with fish skin, the final finishing step

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: כְּלֵי עֵץ מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: They challenged this: Wooden vessels, from when can they become impure?
A bed and a crib: from when he smooths them with fish skin.
And if a bed is strung over its top,
why do I need smoothing with fish skin?
phrases.notes: The straps would cover the wood, so polishing it wouldn't matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כְּלֵי עֵץ מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that a מטה is strung over its frame.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires the bed's wood to be smoothed, which only makes sense if the wood shows. So a bed's straps cannot cover the frame.

steps.title: Both are strung through the frame: holes versus loops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both are strung through the frame. A מטה uses holes in the wood, and a דרגש uses loops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are strung through their own frame. A bed: the straps go in and out through holes. A דרגש: the straps go in and out through loops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes רבי ירמיה's answer to fit the משנה. Both beds are strung through the frame, but in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both are strung through the frame, the wood of both shows, which fits the fish-skin משנה. The difference is now holes for a מטה and loops for a דרגש. This also fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who spoke of untying a דרגש's loops.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both
Bringing in and taking out (the straps)

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: a מטה and a דרגש are both strung through the frame. A מטה uses holes, and a דרגש (a leather bed) uses loops, which can be untied to make it collapse.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are strung through their own body.
A bed: the straps are brought in and out through holes,
a dargash: the straps are brought in and out through loops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the fish-skin משנה by revising רבי ירמיה's distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מטה is strung over its frame, and a דרגש through its frame.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are strung through the frame. A מטה uses holes, and a דרגש uses loops.

steps.title: A bed with protruding posts is just stood on its side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אחא quotes רבי: if a bed has posts sticking up, so it cannot be turned over, standing it on its side is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רבי: a bed whose posts stick out, he stands it up, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more practical rule about overturning beds. If the bed has posts that make it impossible to flip upside down, you just stand it up on its side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual practice is to turn the bed completely over. Here the bed's shape makes that impossible, so רבי rules that standing it on its side does the job. This is a special way of doing it, not a change to the basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Posts on a bed that stick up
And that is enough for him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Acha said that Rebbi said:
A bed whose posts stick out,
he stands it upright, and that is enough for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the mourner's duty to overturn beds (steps 1-2) and adds a practical rule for a bed that cannot be overturned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bed with protruding posts is stood on its side instead of being overturned, and that is enough.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the דרגש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the bed topic with a final ruling: for a דרגש, we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not add a new case. It makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling from step 2 the practical הלכה: a mourner does not have to flip a דרגש, because untying its loops so it collapses is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The bed topic ends here: a bed with posts is stood on its side, and for the דרגש we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: This is his rule from step 2: untie the דרגש's loops and let it fall, with no need to flip it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling that closes the bed discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the דרגש, the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The משנה: a vow against a city or a house
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vows off a city may enter its שבת תחום but not its עיבור. Someone who vows off a house is forbidden only from the doorstop inward.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows off the city may enter the city's boundary, but may not enter its outskirts. But one who vows off a house is forbidden from the doorstop and inward.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how far a נדר against a city or a house reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a city, the נדר covers the city plus its עיבור, the strip right next to it. It does not cover the much larger תחום, the שבת walking zone around the city. For a house, the נדר starts only at the doorstop, so the area outside the door is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Its Shabbos boundary, the 2000-אמה zone around the city
Its outskirts, the small strip right next to the city
Doorstop, where the door closes against

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up עיבור and תחום. The עיבור is a small strip hugging the city and counts as the city. The תחום is the big שבת zone and does not.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who vows off the city —
is permitted to enter the boundary of the city,
phrases.notes: The תחום is the 2000-אמה שבת walking zone around the city.

phrases.english: and is forbidden to enter its outskirts.
phrases.notes: The עיבור is the narrow strip of about seventy אמות right next to the city.

phrases.english: But one who vows off the house —
is forbidden from the doorstop and inward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new topic with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדר against a city includes its עיבור but not its תחום. A נדר against a house begins at the doorstop.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the outskirts count as the city?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that a city's עיבור has the same status as the city itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the outskirts of a city are like the city?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. Why should the strip outside the city count as the city?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treated the עיבור as part of the city for the נדר, even though it lies outside the houses. The גמרא wants a source showing that people call the עיבור by the city's name.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know
that the outskirts of a city are like the city?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling about the עיבור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a city's outskirts count as the city itself.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings the פסוק about יהושע in יריחו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points to the פסוק saying יהושע was 'in יריחו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: because the פסוק says, 'And it was, when יהושע was in יריחו...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers with a פסוק. In the next step the גמרא will explain how this פסוק proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes יהושע as being 'in יריחו.' On its own this proves nothing yet. The proof depends on figuring out where exactly he was standing, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: because the verse says:
"And it was, when Yehoshua was in Yericho, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק that describes יהושע as being 'in יריחו.'

steps.title: יריחו was shut, so יהושע was in its outskirts
steps.stepSummary: יהושע could not have been inside יריחו, which was completely shut. So 'in יריחו' must mean its עיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'in יריחו' mean? If you say actually in יריחו, but it is written, 'And יריחו was shut tight'! Rather, learn from this: in its outskirts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves the point. Since יריחו was locked up, 'in יריחו' must mean just outside it, in the עיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first tries to read 'in יריחו' as inside the city. Another פסוק says the city was sealed shut, so יהושע could not be inside. Yet the תנ״ך still says he was 'in יריחו', which shows the עיבור is called by the city's name.
steps.whatToRemember: The עיבור counts as the city, because יהושע stood outside the sealed יריחו and the פסוק still says he was 'in יריחו.'

phrases.english: What does "in Yericho" mean?
If you say actually inside Yericho,
but it is written: "And Yericho was completely shut"!
Rather, learn from this: he was in its outskirts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוחנן's פסוק proves that the עיבור counts as the city.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that the עיבור has the status of the city.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 5:13 read together with יהושע 6:1: the city was sealed, yet יהושע is called 'in יריחו.'

steps.title: Maybe even the שבת boundary counts as the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe יהושע was further out, in the תחום, and even the תחום counts as the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe יהושע was in the תחום, which would mean the תחום also counts as the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only shows that יהושע was outside the sealed city. It doesn't say how far out. If he was in the תחום, then a נדר against a city should forbid the תחום too, which goes against the משנה.

phrases.english: Say that it means even in its boundary!
phrases.notes: The challenge is that maybe יהושע was even further out, and the פסוק still called that 'in יריחו.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 13 by suggesting it proves too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from יריחו and the משנה's ruling that the תחום is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows only that יהושע was outside the city, maybe as far as the תחום. Then the תחום would count as the city and should be forbidden too.

steps.title: The תורה calls the תחום 'outside the city'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה describes the תחום as 'outside the city,' so the תחום is not part of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written about its boundary: 'And you shall measure outside the city'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A פסוק calls the תחום 'outside the city,' so it cannot count as the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about measuring the תחום calls it 'outside the city.' So the תחום is clearly not the city. That leaves only the עיבור as the place where יהושע was still called 'in יריחו,' and the משנה's line between עיבור and תחום holds.
steps.whatToRemember: The עיבור counts as the city (from יריחו), but the תחום does not, because the תורה calls it 'outside the city.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the exact line in the משנה: a נדר against a city reaches the עיבור but stops before the תחום.

phrases.english: But it is written about its boundary:
"And you shall measure outside the city."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that places the תחום outside the city
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe 'in יריחו' could stretch as far as the תחום, so the תחום would count as the city.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה calls the תחום 'outside the city,' so only the עיבור counts as the city.

steps.title: A vow against a house covers only the doorstop and inward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule for someone who vows not to enter a house and draws an inference from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who vows not to enter 'the house' is only forbidden from the doorstop and inward. This means that from the doorstop and outward, he is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about a vow not to enter a house. It also points out what the rule implies, which sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line that matters is the אֲגַף, the doorstop where the closed door rests. Everything inside it counts as 'the house.' Everything outside it does not, even the space right under the lintel. That second point is what רב מרי will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow (here, a vow not to enter something)
The doorstop, the line where the door closes

phrases.english: One who vows that the house is forbidden to him

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא מִן הָאֲגַף וְלִפְנִים.
phrases.english: is forbidden only from the doorstop and inward.
But from the doorstop and outward, he is not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the city and עיבור discussion in steps 11-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against a house covers only the area from the doorstop inward. The space outside the doorstop, including under the lintel, is not 'the house.'

steps.title: A ברייתא about a house with צרעת says standing under the lintel is still 'in the house'
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי brings a ברייתא showing that a כהן standing under the lintel has not yet left the house. This suggests the space under the lintel counts as part of the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי objected: The פסוק says 'And the כהן shall go out from the house.' One might think he can go to his own home and declare the house closed off from there. So the פסוק says 'to the entrance of the house.' If it is 'to the entrance,' one might think he can stand under the lintel and close it off from there. So the פסוק says 'from the house,' meaning he must go out of the entire house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי challenges the משנה using a ברייתא about a כהן closing off a house with צרעת. According to that ברייתא, standing under the lintel still counts as being inside the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two words of the פסוק against each other. 'To the entrance' means he cannot go far away. 'From the house' means he cannot stand under the lintel, because there he has not fully left the house. So the space under the lintel is treated as 'the house,' which clashes with step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Closing off (quarantining) a house with a suspected נגע
The lintel, the beam above the doorway
'One might think... so the פסוק says,' the standard way a ברייתא learns from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never says out loud what the problem is. The point is this: under the lintel is outside the doorstop, yet the ברייתא says he is still 'in the house' there. That contradicts the משנה in step 16.

phrases.english: רב מרי raised an objection:
"And the כהן shall go out from the house"
One might think he may go to his own home and close off the house from there.
So the פסוק says: "to the entrance of the house."
If he must be at the entrance of the house,
one might think he may stand under the lintel and close it off.
So the פסוק says: "from the house,"
meaning not until he goes out of the entire house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the implication of step 16 that the area outside the doorstop is not 'the house.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 16 that from the doorstop outward, including under the lintel, is not 'the house.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a כהן under the lintel has not yet left 'the house,' so the space under the lintel counts as the house.

steps.title: The ברייתא's practical rule: stand beside the doorway, though even other spots work after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. Ideally the כהן stands beside the doorway outside. But if he closed off the house from his own home or from under the lintel, it still works after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? He stands beside the doorframe and closes off the house. And how do we know that if he went to his own home and closed it off, or stood under the lintel and closed it off, the closing still counts? Because the פסוק says 'and he shall close off the house,' which means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the same ברייתא רב מרי quoted. It gives the ideal way to do it and adds that the other ways still work after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally, the כהן stands just outside, next to the doorway. The ברייתא adds that other spots still work after the fact (בדיעבד), based on the words 'and he shall close off the house.' This part does not add to the challenge. The challenge still rests on the ideal rule that under the lintel is not 'outside the house.'

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, no matter what
His closing off counts as valid

phrases.english: How so?
He stands beside the doorframe and closes off the house.
And how do we know that if he went to his own home and closed it off,
or stood under the lintel and closed it off,
that his closing off still counts?
The פסוק says: "and he shall close off the house,"
which means in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that רב מרי quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Same target as step 17: the משנה's doorstop line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא still treats under the lintel as not yet 'outside the house' in the ideal case.

steps.title: A house with נגעים is different because the פסוק says 'from the house'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule about נגעים is special. The פסוק demands leaving the whole house, so it tells us nothing about vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different with a house of נגעים, because it is written 'from the house,' meaning not until he goes out of the entire house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב מרי. The ברייתא's rule comes from a special phrase in the פסוק about נגעים, so it does not apply to vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, the space under the lintel is not 'the house,' just as the משנה says. With נגעים, the פסוק adds an extra demand ('from the house') that he leave the entire house, including the doorway area. So the two sources do not contradict each other. The נגעים rule is a special requirement of that פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: For vows, 'the house' means only from the doorstop inward. The stricter rule for a house with נגעים comes from the special wording 'from the house' and does not change the vow rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא separates the plain meaning of a word ('house') from a special rule that a פסוק sets for one area of הלכה.

phrases.english: It is different with a house
phrases.notes: He means a house with נגעים (צרעת), the case in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: because it is written: "from the house,"
meaning not until he goes out of the entire house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרי's challenge from steps 17-18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the נגעים rule comes from a special phrase in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that under the lintel is generally part of 'the house.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Under the lintel is generally not 'the house.' With נגעים only, the פסוק requires leaving the entire house.
